limitations: Source selection is a native workflow root. Conversation-only threads need an explicit turn/input selection contract and are not accepted as workflow test sources.
Targets are published workflow profiles or saved unpublished definition revisions with an allowed ordinary worker profile. The API accepts references, not raw scripts or configuration overrides.
The advanced form uses registered IDs and explicit execution identity; it does not edit source or provide a new general authoring surface.
Reservations with pending admission are retried explicitly with the same key. No automatic boot queue, snapshot restore or exactly-once guarantee is claimed.
The test project supplies files, relative workflow sources, current MCP access and execution-owner credentials. Source files/credentials are not cloned or frozen.
Revoking source read authority hides provenance on further reads; already-admitted copied inputs/results cannot be recalled. Execution remains under current test-project/profile authority.
A test record state of started describes admission. Current execution state and results come from native workflow history.
Docker uses stock Qwen and a deterministic model fixture, not corporate harness authorization.
verificationNotes: The real migrated-SQLite/native plugin integration covers owner/reviewer/admin source access, independent project/profile execution authorization, explicit admin execution owner, forbidden caller input/cwd/UID fields, exact string and JSON capture, pinned draft/published snapshots, idempotency conflict after draft revision update, foreign record denial and provenance loss after source revocation.

UI regressions exercise lost admission response retry with the same key, exact request references without replacement input, reopening provenance by native run ID, pinned revision/profile labels and navigation to the source.

The existing private native agent-workflow admission accepts JSON arguments through its existing bounded native validation. Published string requests retain their contract; publication itself still requires text input/output metadata. No host wire or public Plugin SDK surface changed.

An initial profile-publication fixture omitted required text input/output metadata; the fixture now follows the actual publication contract. Draft tests use the separate administrative exact-revision reader rather than applying publication-only restrictions.
The initially unused owner index was removed by regenerating the uncommitted migration/snapshot through Drizzle; production snapshots were not manually edited.
Final readonly provenance labels and CLI guide text are added after the composite image was built; focused UI checks and a final image rebuild verify/package those additions.

The full Docker composite passed all 63 Turbo tasks (745181 ms), including published/draft/JSON tests, actual test UID/HOME/cwd, UI creation from an inspected source, provenance rediscovery without its original URL pointer, source navigation, native restart and crash recovery. Final snapshot-label text, CLI guide regeneration and the unused-index migration cleanup are included in a subsequent image rebuild; final migrated-SQLite and focused UI checks cover those changes.

Final focused checks also simulate loss of the native admission response after root creation, then recover the same reservation/native ID; reject disabled draft definitions and unknown query fields; and retain normal historical reads. Those admission/query restrictions are included in the final rebuilt image after the passing composite. No conforming composite request changed.

The final native-SQLite case also starts an administrator-selected test under Bob from Alice's inspected input and verifies the actual core workflow binding belongs to Bob/test project, while an ungranted profile still fails. This distinguishes explicit execution identity from source ownership.
